comment: The TCP relay's hosts (docs/relay.md): the backend's /relay connects only to these, on port 443, for a TLS client that names the same host. The page reads it too: `fetch` lists the hosts it reaches by its own fetch() (they send CORS headers), not by the relay. A host goes one way for all its paths (the TLS is the page's own, so the relay never sees them): api.anthropic.com's Messages API sends CORS headers, but Claude Code's /api/claude_code/settings there does not. A Node.js process's https.request and fetch know the path before they connect: `fetch_paths` lists those (exactly, without the query) that go by fetch() all the same.
